requirements.text: The NLM Digital Repository must be designed with regard to international best practice for digital archives/repositories.
The NLM Digital Repository must support the acceptance and preservation of material that is provided in non-preferred formats or non-standard formats.
The system design and architecture should minimize duplicate data entry of any metadata for objects in the NLM Digital Repository.
The Repository must support the use of multiple languages and non-Roman scripts for ingest, maintenance and access of digital objects and associated metadata.
The Repository system must follow HHS/NIH standards concerning software and systems security.
To the extent possible, automation should be used for the extraction of descriptive and technical metadata.
The system must support the bulk ingest of material as well as ingest of individual objects.
The repository system must include the ability to record all actions and decisions made concerning the submitted material.
The Library will not provide offline delivery services.

The NLM Digital Repository must implement security controls compliant with NIST SP 800-53 (Moderate baseline) and FIPS 140-2/3 for all cryptographic modules, with annual independent security assessments.
The repository must implement rate limiting and traffic shaping to protect against automated scraping and DoS attacks while maintaining a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
The system must provide a search response time of less than 2 seconds for 95% of queries under normal load.

The system must perform automated integrity checks (e.g., fixity checks) on all stored objects at least annually, with a target recovery time objective (RTO) of [X] hours and recovery point objective (RPO) of [Y] hours.
The administrative GUI must allow NLM staff to perform manual quality control tasks with no more than [X] clicks per object and provide clear error feedback for failed ingestions.
Define specific latency targets, such as: 'The system shall return search results for 95% of queries in under 2 seconds under a load of 50 concurrent users.'

Specify a performance requirement for bulk operations, such as: 'The system shall support the ingest of at least 100GB of data per hour without impacting the performance of concurrent search and retrieval operations.'
Define a maximum response time for federated queries, such as: 'Federated search results shall be aggregated and displayed within 5 seconds, even when querying multiple remote repository sites.'

OPEN: The PRD mentions the need for granular access control but does not specify the authentication mechanism or identity management integration. - The repository must integrate with the NLM/NIH enterprise identity and access management (IAM) system using standardized protocols such as SAML 2.0 or OIDC for authentication.

OPEN: The PRD does not specify the expected volume of data, number of objects, or concurrent user load. - The system must support the ingest and management of at least [X] terabytes of data and [Y] million objects, with concurrent access for [Z] users.

OPEN: The PRD lacks projected data volume, growth rates, or throughput requirements for ingest and retrieval. - Define expected annual growth in terabytes and peak concurrent user counts to inform storage and compute architecture sizing.
